_comment: Copy to config.json (git-ignored) or run `harness init`. Every value here is a placeholder or a default.

fixHints.hint: In an .astro file, a component's props are Astro.props, for example: const { block } = Astro.props;
In an .astro page, route parameters are Astro.params.
In .astro markup this usually means an expression { ... } or a .map(...) block is not closed: every { needs its }, every ( its ).
An element opened inside an { ... } expression must also be closed inside it.
The content loader is called glob: import { glob } from "astro/loaders";
astro:content exists only inside Astro's own build. astro.config must not import src/content.config.ts: a collection needs no entry in astro.config.

fixHints.match: Do you need to install type definitions for node
fixHints.hint: This project has no Node type definitions and nothing may be installed. Remove the node: import; to render a component in a test, use experimental_AstroContainer from "astro/container".

reviewNotes: Astro escapes {expression} output in markup; only set:html inserts raw HTML.
An .astro file's frontmatter (between the --- lines) runs on the server; browser code goes in a <script> tag.
Component props are Astro.props; a bare props is an undefined name.

A request body from request.json() can be any JSON value, including a number, a string or null: check it is an object before using in, Reflect.has or property access, or the route answers 500 instead of 400.
A form field or editor wired to a callback (such as onChange) must call it on every change, or the edit is never saved.

A content collection lives in src/content.config.ts: import { defineCollection } from "astro:content"; import { glob } from "astro/loaders"; import { z } from "astro/zod"; export const collections = { blog: defineCollection({ loader: glob({ pattern: "*.md", base: "./src/content/blog" }), schema: z.object({ ... }) }) };

Read a collection with getCollection("blog") from "astro:content". An entry has id and data. Render one with const { Content } = await render(entry), render also coming from "astro:content". Entries have no slug.

An API route exports its method by name: import type { APIRoute } from "astro"; export const GET: APIRoute = () => new Response(JSON.stringify(body), { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } }); add export const prerender = false; when the route must not be prerendered. A test imports GET and calls it directly.
A dynamic page such as src/pages/[lang]/index.astro exports getStaticPaths, returning [{ params: { lang } }], and reads Astro.params.

To test an .astro component: import { experimental_AstroContainer } from "astro/container"; const container = await experimental_AstroContainer.create(); const html = await container.renderToString(Component, { props: { ... } }); Import the component by its path, with the .astro extension.
astro:content exists only inside Astro's own build: plain test code cannot import a file that imports it. Put logic that needs testing in a file that does not.
node_modules cannot be read. Do not look for an API there, and do not write throwaway test files to find out what a package exports: use these facts and the code in the repository.
